notes.C01: Exact event logs for own screen repros skip perception entirely, but only cover the recorder-wrapped case.
notes.C02: Pixel-to-action-script plus test compile is a research project; feasibility is low and the cursor/OCR detectors will need ongoing tuning.
notes.C03: Cheap falsifiable bet on reusing existing signals, but it is unproven whether vision models can read these images.
notes.C04: Directly closes the named audio gap with local tools, low cost and a clear first step.
notes.C05: Sound-and-visual coincidence is a sharp cause anchor, but it only helps a narrow set of events.
notes.C06: Boundary pairs plus a narrow look call give the best temporal signal per token and extend the existing look verb.
notes.C07: Lazy question-driven sensing cuts cost, but it adds a ledger and router to maintain and depends on good agent questions.
notes.C08: Delivers the run-daily-without-thinking goal through a hook and tiers, but the tiers, versioning and GPU sync raise maintenance.
notes.C09: A cheap proof that doubles as a self-test, and it lets every other claim be measured.
notes.C10: Honest gaps and budgeted zones are good discipline, but it is a format layer and not a new sense.
notes.C11: Only paid and egress option; it justifies cost only by doubt and breaks the local-first default unless it stays opt-in.
notes.C12: Subagent viewers save main context, but they spend tokens per use and the crossover claim is unverified.
notes.C13: Priming defence is a niche worry that the brief does not raise.
notes.C14: Slow-change channel is an edge-case audit with small value for daily use.
notes.C15: Saliency ranking is a plausible budget heuristic, but it has little evidence behind it.
